rationale: Stands. The native app takes the mobile SDKs, which Microsoft strongly recommends and which support push through Azure Notification Hub. The back-end relay takes Messaging APIs, which are for service-to-service work and not recommended from a user's device. The website code takes the Live chat SDK, whose getAgentAvailability returns isQueueAvailable and is named for deciding whether the start conversation option is visible. I tested every token on every row. The strongest alternative is Direct Line for the relay. It fails for a documented reason: the custom messaging channel page names Direct Line as a custom channel and lists a Bot Framework agent registered with Azure Bot Service as a prerequisite, and the Direct Line sample needs a Direct Line secret and bot handle. The stem forbids that registration, while Messaging API setup needs only a Microsoft Entra app registration. "Internally attached" on the Direct Line page describes the bot inside Contact Center, not an exemption. Checks 16 and 21: both stem constraints need product knowledge to apply, and the native and back-end rows each turn on a fact the token names don't give. The representative availability APIs (GA April 30, 2026 in the archived wave 1 plan) aren't a token and change no row. Distinct from ab250-d2-q14 and ab250-d2-q15, which test how to use one surface. Row 3 shares the getAgentAvailability fact with q10 option b, but the decision differs.
